title: RAW planet-child event attribution versus multi-source properties and predominant naming
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. The Md2 general conclusion separates birth/conception attribution, multiple planetary property contributions and predominant naming with birth/day/hour qualification. Preserve different event/order roles, rare sole power and unresolved scope; no numeric weights or target values.

design.unit: Complete planetary conclusion271vB5–32, a visibly separate general paragraph following the Luna article. Its backward reference is to the7-planet chapter; no claim the other5planet articles have been newly read.
design.mechanism: Maintain an event-indexed attribution record, a provenance-indexed received-property profile and a naming record as linked but non-identical roles of the same person. Do not collapse strongest planet at an event, largest received share and birth/day/hour ruler into one unqualified head.
source_argument: A person is called a planet's child under birth OR conception at a time of strong eastern-rising power; the strongest planet claims the child and gives properties according to nature.
Sole planetary power is described as rare. Multiple properties are received, with2,3orall planets as examples and little/much from each.
Naming is stated from the greatest received properties, together with a birth-under-planet and day/hour clause. The exact conjunction and temporal indexing remain unresolved.

records.EVENT_ATTRIBUTION: (person,event_kind,event,planet,eastern_rising,power_comparison). Event kind is BIRTH or CONCEPTION and must stay attached to that record.
records.RECEIVED_PROFILE: (person,reference_scope,{planet -> received property bundle},share_comparison). Contributions retain their planet provenance; no arithmetic sum or biological parenthood.
records.NAMING: (person,name_source_planet,received_profile,birth_reference,time_qualification). Naming is a classification, not the whole support set.

fixed_role_laws: A property contribution from q does not by itself make q the predominant name source.
The name source must belong to the contribution support under the chosen naming scope.
Comparing power at an episode and comparing received properties are distinct ordinal relations; neither equality nor common units are supplied.
Birth and conception are separate episodes of one person, not aliases or freely interchangeable dates.
Day and hour qualification must retain its stated planet/reference; a timing clause is not a numerical share.
Rarity of a planet holding sole power is not identical to a hard cardinality rule for a person's property contributors. Preserve both assertions without identifying the two sets.
explicit_open_choices: Birth/conception OR can be an alternative reference procedure or a disjunctive condition. Do not pool two charts/events without a newly counted aggregation rule.
The final birth/day/hour condition may restrict the same name-source planet, or delimit the earlier attribution rule. A chosen whole-reading branch must state which.
The generic multi-contribution assertion and examples2/3/all do not certify that only counts2,3,7 occur;4–6 are not excluded by a fabricated exhaustive list.
If a strict at-least-two property-support rule is selected from the generic prose, count its quantifier force separately; sole-power rarity does not automatically violate or establish it.
An order-preserving power-to-share map, identical maxima and a unique maximum all need separate scope/scale assumptions if required.

prospective_cases.premises: Persons p and r each have contributions from planets A and B; written received-share comparisons favor A for p and B for r.
prospective_cases.consequence: Support queries agree, naming records differ. This is not only substituting7planet constants for570's4complexions because the records also retain event and timing roles.

prospective_cases.premises: The birth record favors A in power, conception record favors B.
prospective_cases.consequence: Event-indexed attributions differ without contradiction. A frozen choice of birth versus conception can change the selected attribution; the final naming record cannot be resolved by silently switching event.

prospective_cases.premises: A stated power comparison and a stated received-property comparison refer to different scopes or respects.
prospective_cases.consequence: Do not identify their maxima without a bridge. This is not a claim that contrary rankings are historically attested or that the source's dependence on strength is meaningless.

design.case_status: Declared logical examples only, not named natal cases observed in the text or target. No arbitrary numerical sample weights are assigned.
serious_rivals: One planet completely owns the human and transmits all properties; this loses the explicit multi-source qualification.
One event/one scalar determines rising power, all received shares and the name; potentially compatible if a common-scale/event bridge is assumed, but not automatic.
Birth and conception are two alternative schools of attribution, not two concurrently contributing events. This may be fully compatible with the source and must remain explicit.
A conventional generic type-name exposition makes no claim about an individual's exhaustive measured profile; do not manufacture observed patient records.
design.falsifier: A future whole-reading contract fails if it changes the common person, swaps birth/conception or power/share orderings without writing, names a planet outside its claimed support, or erases the birth/day/hour qualification to obtain one winner. If both source branches yield the same available written claims, retain equivalence rather than preference. No complete target contract or test exists yet.
